prompts: Finance has to chase June's receivables. The invoices, the bank statement and our reconciliation notes are in {WS}/backoffice. What do we still have to collect or fix? Record it in {WS}/result.json: unpaid and duplicated (invoice ids) and mismatched (id, invoiced, paid).
answers:
[goal] Reconcile June invoices against the bank statement and write the chase list to `./result.json`.

[action] Parsed `backoffice/invoices.csv` (40 invoices) and `backoffice/bank_statement_june.csv` (41 lines) with a script at `tmp/reconcile.py`; normalized every memo format (`inv1007`, `INV-1015`, `invoice 1023`), applied the README's exclusive priority unpaid > duplicated > mismatched, then re-verified each invoice with an independent pass.

[result] `./result.json`:

```json
{
  "unpaid": ["INV-1008", "INV-1030", "INV-1033"],
  "duplicated": ["INV-1015"],
  "mismatched": [
    {"id": "INV-1021", "invoiced": 21320.36, "paid": 21070.36},
    {"id": "INV-1036", "invoiced": 8619.16, "paid": 7757.24}
  ]
}
```

- Unpaid: INV-1008 Coruja Labs 23,693.91; INV-1030 Vetor BI 8,092.29; INV-1033 Arena Studio 21,266.69 (no bank line at all).
- Duplicated: INV-1015 Ateliê Norte received twice, 1,904.29 on 06-05 and again on 06-17 ("resend") — refund/credit one.
- Mismatched: INV-1021 short 250.00; INV-1036 short 861.92.
- Ignored per README: unidentified PIX 1,500.00, CDB interest 1,204.33, bank fee -89.90.

How I know it is right: 40 invoice rows + 41 bank rows close out exactly — 38 invoice-referencing payments, 3 explicitly ignorable lines, 0 bank memos pointing at a non-existent invoice id, and only these 6 invoices fail a strict one-payment-at-exact-amount test. The independent second pass reproduced the same 6 anomalies with no other deviations, and every other invoice matched one payment to the cent.

Assumptions: invoice numbers in memos are the 4-digit `inv`/`invoice` tokens; amounts must match to the cent; README exclusivity means a duplicated invoice is reported only as duplicated; mismatch amounts are JSON numbers in BRL.
